about: The `town_meeting_votes` table, published whole. See /api/schema for its grain. This file is fy 2023 only.

rows.subject: Accept the annual reports of Town officers and committees
rows.quote: VOTED UNANIMOUS CONSENT (to Pass Over having already accepted the regular written reports of the Town Officers and Committees).

rows.subject: Reauthorize revolving funds for various town departments
rows.quote: VOTED UNANIMOUS CONSENT to re-authorize the revolving funds for certain town departments, boards, committees, agencies or officers for the spending limits as follows:

rows.subject: Transfer funds for payment of prior year expenses
rows.quote: VOTED (99 YES, 4 NO) to transfer the sum of $4,000 from Free Cash for payment of prior year expenses.

rows.subject: Amend the FY2023 budget via multiple line-item transfers
rows.quote: VOTED (100 YES, 6 NO) to transfer from line #5/Workers Compensation the sum of $25,377.77; transfer from #29/Technology Department the sum of $14,229.73; transfer from line #13/Reserve Fund the sum of $75,000; transfer from line #40/Police Lockup the sum of $33,184.96;

rows.subject: Transfer funds to the Overlay Account for FY2023 abatements
rows.quote: VOTED (98 YES, 12NO) to transfer from Free Cash the sum of $1,500,000 to the Overlay Account for all anticipated costs associated with FY 2023 abatements.

rows.subject: Fund the FY2024 Capital Plan
rows.quote: VOTED (103YES, 6 NO) to raise and appropriate the sum of $556,789.09; transfer from Free Cash the sum of $467,268.98; transfer from Article 14 of the 5/2/15 Annual Town Meeting the sum of $8,800.26;

rows.subject: Fund first year of firefighters' collective bargaining agreement
rows.quote: VOTED (98 YES, 3 NO) to transfer from Article 7 of the 5/6/23 Annual Town Meeting, line #13A/Salary Reserve the sum of $26,022.69 to fund the first year of the FY24 -FY26 Collective Bargaining Agreement dated July 1, 2023

rows.subject: Adopt FY2024 Salary Administration Plan schedule and fund wage increases
rows.quote: VOTED (86 YES, 7 NO) to replace the current Salary Schedule in Chapter 70, Section 70-8.A, the Salary Administration Plan of the General Bylaws, with a  FY 2024 Salary Schedule as recommended by the Personnel Committee as printed in the Annual Town Meeting Warrant Booklet,

rows.subject: Transfer funds to the Stabilization Fund
rows.quote: VOTED UNANIMOUS CONSENT to transfer from Free Cash the sum of $100,000 to the Stabilization Fund.

rows.subject: Transfer funds to the Special Purpose Stabilization Fund
rows.quote: VOTED (63 YES, 26 NO) to transfer from Free Cash the sum of $250,000 to the Special Purpose Stabilization fund.

rows.subject: Transfer funds into the OPEB Trust Fund
rows.quote: VOTED (69 YES, 19 NO) to transfer from Free Cash the sum of $282,855, and transfer from Sewer Enterprise Retained Earnings the sum of $1,000.00 to the OPEB Trust Fund established at the November 30, 2010 Special Town Meeting.

rows.subject: Create the Opioid Settlement Stabilization Fund and deposit settlement proceeds
rows.quote: VOTED (80 YES, 11 NO), pursuant to the provisions of G.L. c.40, Section 5B, to create a new special purpose stabilization fund, to be known as the Opioid Settlement Stabilization Fund, for dedication, without further appropriation, of 100% of opioid litigation settlement

rows.subject: Appropriate funds to operate the Sewer Enterprise Fund for FY2024
rows.quote: VOTED (72 YES, 8 NO) to appropriate  from Sewer Enterprise revenues the sum of  $89,891.85; transfer from the  Inflow/Infiltration Stabilization Fund the sum of $9,900.00; transfer from the Sewer Capital Reserve Stabilization Fund the sum of $35,000.00;

rows.subject: Transfer funds into the Sewer Capital Reserve Stabilization Fund
rows.quote: VOTED UNANIMOUS CONSENT to transfer from Sewer Enterprise Retained Earnings the sum of $36,621.37 into the Sewer Capital Reserve Stabilization Fund.

rows.subject: Petition the General Court for a means-tested senior citizen property tax exemption
rows.quote: VOTED (77 YES, 11 NO) [with amendment (passing 74 to9) to eliminate "residential" in the 2nd sentence of Section 3] to authorize the Board of Selectmen, on behalf of the Town, to petition the General Court for the enactment of special legislation

rows.subject: Amend the zoning bylaw to add a Self-Storage use category
rows.quote: VOTED (66 YES, 8 NO – 50 needed for 2/3rds majority) to amend the Code of Lunenburg, Section 250-4.1, which is a Section of the Protective Bylaw entitled Permitted and Prohibited Uses", by adding a new section 250-4.1 K(20) entitled "Self-Storage," and inserting the same into the accompanying "Use Tables".

rows.subject: Amend the FY2024 budget with additional appropriations to several town lines
rows.quote: VOTED (126 YES, 13 NO 93 needed for 2/3rds majority) to raise and appropriate the sum of $319,000 as follows: to line #13/Reserve Fund, the sum of $200,000; to line#13A Salary Reserve, the sum of $99,000; to line #31/Town Clerk Salary, the sum of $20,000;

rows.subject: Appropriate funds for payment of prior year expenses
rows.quote: VOTED (9/10ths DECLARED) to raise and appropriate the sum of $1,423.52 for payment of prior year expenses.

rows.subject: Fund first year of AFSCME municipal employees' collective bargaining agreement
rows.quote: VOTED (132 YES, 11 NO) to transfer from Article 7 of the May 6, 2023 Annual Town Meeting, line #13A/Salary Reserve, the sum of $58,431.03 to fund the first year of the FY 24, FY 25, and FY 26 Lunenburg Municipal Employees Collective Bargaining Agreement dated July 1, 2023

rows.subject: Transfer Special Purpose Stabilization funds for a new ambulance and two dump trucks
rows.quote: ARTICLE 4 WAS DEFEATED (29 YES, 92 NO)

rows.subject: Transfer Opioid Settlement funds for the Police Department's Mental Health Co-Response program
rows.quote: VOTED (125 YES, 2 NO  85 needed for 2/3rds majority) to transfer the sum of $80,000 from the Opioid Settlement Stabilization Fund to be used to fund the Police Department’s Mental Health Co-Response program,

rows.subject: Transfer FY23 Capital Plan funds to the school district for HVAC at the Primary School
rows.quote: VOTED (104 YES, 16 NO) to transfer the sum of $232,800 from the FY23 Capital Plan, as voted under Article 6 of the May 7, 2022 Annual Town Meeting, to the Lunenburg School District for the purpose of installing ductless split climate control systems at the Lunenburg Primary School.

rows.subject: Transfer sewer funds into the Sewer Reserve Capacity Stabilization Fund
rows.quote: VOTED UNANIMOUS  (but one) CONSENT to transfer the sum of $1,851.30 from Sewer Enterprise Retained Earnings to the Sewer Reserve Capacity Stabilization Fund.

rows.subject: Transfer sewer funds into the Sewer Inflow/Infiltration Stabilization Fund
rows.quote: VOTED UNANIMOUS  (but one) CONSENT to transfer the sum of $5,340.00 from Sewer Enterprise Retained Earnings to the Sewer Inflow/Infiltration Stabilization Fund.

rows.subject: Rewrite the Water Supply Protection District zoning bylaw
rows.quote: AR TICLE 9 WAS PASSED OVER (80 YES, 29 NO)

rows.subject: Hear an interim report from the Municipal Building Design Committee
rows.quote: ARTICLE 10 W AS P ASSED OVER (UNANIMOUS VOICE VOTE)

rows.subject: Fund repairs to a portion of the TC Passios Building roof
rows.quote: VOTED (81 YES, 11 NO ) to transfer the sum of $300,000 from the FY23 Capital Plan, as voted under Article 6 of the May 7, 2022 Annual Town Meeting, to fund repairs to a portion of the TC Passios Building roof, located at 1025 Massachusetts Avenue.

rows.subject: Reauthorize Marshall Park engineering/design funds and dedicate the site to recreation
rows.quote: VOTED (90 YES, 4 NO  63 needed for 2/3rds majority) to: (i) to reauthorize raising and appropriating of the sum of $184,000 for final engineering and design services for certain recreation and open space areas at the property known as Marshall Park,

rows.subject: Amend the zoning bylaw definition of "Farm" for agricultural use
rows.quote: VOTED (81 YES, 2 NO  56 needed for 2/3rds majority) to amend the Code of Lunenburg, Chapter 250, being the Protective Bylaw, also entitled "Zoning".

rows.subject: Add solar parking canopy special permit provisions to the zoning bylaw
rows.quote: VOTED (62 YES, 6 NO  45 needed for 2/3rds majority) to amend the Code of Lunenburg, Sections 250-4.5 and 250-4.6, which are Sections of the Protective Bylaw entitled "Commercial District" and "Office Park/Industrial District," respectively,
